# Cross-Domain Analogy Cases

Every scenario below is invented for regression testing.

## CASE-07 — Attractive Metaphor Without Prediction

A microbial community is called a “distributed computer,” but no components,
failure modes, or distinct predictions are mapped.

Expected: `METAPHOR ONLY`; narrative use at most; not scientific novelty.

## CASE-08 — Strong Mapping With Invalidating Mismatch

A battery electrode is mapped to an ecological resource network. Nodes and
flows map cleanly, but the analogy requires resource reproduction while charge
is conserved and cannot reproduce.

Expected: mismatch stated explicitly; `INVALID ANALOGY` or `USEFUL HEURISTIC
ONLY`; the invalid transfer cannot become a mechanism.

## CASE-09 — Mapping With Discriminating Prediction

A threshold controller is structurally mapped to a synthetic sensor: multiple
weak inputs integrate, cross a threshold, trigger output, and delayed feedback
raises the next threshold. The mapped model uniquely predicts history-dependent
threshold elevation after a pulse, while the baseline predicts full reset.

Expected: `NEW DISCRIMINATING PREDICTION`; eligible for candidate evaluation;
still requires the Scientific Coherence Firewall.

## Required Analogy Invariants

Every promotable analogy includes a domain-independent structural signature,
explicit component/relationship mapping, mismatch analysis, unsafe-transfer
list, prediction delta or explanatory leverage, provenance, and literature
novelty `NOT VERIFIED` unless separately checked.
